$comment: saydo/status is the compact verdict an MCP client or agent reads at tool-selection time to gate a tool. It is derived deterministically from a signed receipt and carries a pointer back to it. It is a convenience, never a trust root: the proof is the receipt named in `receipt`, which anyone verifies without trusting SayDo.
title: SayDo tool status

verdict.$comment: warranted: conformant AND signed AND at least one invariant about the tool's conduct was demonstrated. failing: a declared behavior was refuted, or a finding was raised. inconclusive: nothing failed and nothing was established -- the tool did no observable work, so it has not been shown to be well behaved, only unobserved; this is the ordinary result for a server that declines to act without credentials, and it is NOT a weaker pass. draft: tested but unsigned. revoked: the claim was withdrawn after the receipt was issued; the receipt is still authentic and no longer current. expired: the last check is too old to describe what is installed today. unknown: no receipt exists. An agent treats anything but 'warranted' as not-vouched-for.

summary.$comment: One line, written to be read the same way by a model and a person.

advice.$comment: A directive an agent can act on. Refusal-first: anything short of 'warranted' advises caution or refusal.

envelope.$comment: The behavioral promises that held, in plain words: 'makes no network calls', 'writes no files', etc. This is what an agent may rely on.

caveat.$comment: The observation limit, compact. States that behavior was observed, not sandboxed.

checkedHere.$comment: False: the status does not itself verify the signature. Verification happens against the receipt, by the consumer, so the status stays untrusted.

trust.$comment: States plainly that the status is a convenience and the receipt is the evidence.
